findings.source_quote: ἄκουε, φησί, καὶ τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν γυναικῶν τῶν τὰ ἱμάτια μέλανα ἐχουσῶν.
findings.english_quote: “Listen also,” he said, “to the names of the women wearing black garments.
findings.issue: The translation follows the selected working reading, but its notes do not disclose the supplied apparatus's distinction at this occurrence: ἱμάτια is attributed to Hilgenfeld's conjecture, compared with L₁, L₂ and E, whereas A reportedly reads ὀνόματα. Footnote [a] addresses the opening insertion, not this separate editorial choice in paragraph 3. Readers therefore cannot distinguish this conjectural working wording from the reported Athos reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “black garments” in the main text. Add a paragraph-3 textual note stating that the supplied project transcription of the printed apparatus attributes “garments” to Hilgenfeld's conjecture, compared with L₁, L₂ and E, and reports “names” in A. Explicitly attribute the report rather than presenting it as fresh manuscript verification. Review the proposed note before acceptance.

findings.source_quote: καὶ εἰ μὴ ταῦτα τὰ πνεύματα μετ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐσχήκει⸢σαν⸣, ⸢οὐκ ἂν⸣ εὔχρηστοι γεγόνεισαν τῇ οἰκοδομῇ τοῦ πύργου τούτου.
findings.english_quote: The printed Athos-based text reconstructs the negative “would not” in damage.
findings.issue: Footnote [f] appropriately distinguishes the supplied negative from surviving text, but does not disclose the separate editorial choice in the same conditional: the supplied apparatus attributes γεγόνεισαν to Anger's conjecture and reports γεγόνασι in A. Its account of the final clause's textual basis is consequently incomplete at a specifically supplied apparatus locus.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand [f] to report, with attribution to the supplied apparatus transcription, that the working predicate γεγόνεισαν is Anger's conjecture and A is reported as reading γεγόνασι. Explain the differing verb forms without claiming that the reported variant cancels the negative or requires changing the selected counterfactual translation. Retain the main text pending fresh review of any proposed replacement.

findings.source_quote: ἄκουε, φησί, καὶ τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν γυναικῶν τῶν τὰ ἱμάτια μέλανα ἐχουσῶν.
findings.english_quote: He said, “Now listen to the names of the women dressed in black.
findings.issue: “Dressed in black” faithfully represents the selected garments reading, but the simplified edition independently inherits an undisclosed editorial choice. The supplied apparatus reports ἱμάτια as Hilgenfeld's conjecture, compared with L₁, L₂ and E, and ὀνόματα as A's reading. Its opening note does not disclose this separate paragraph-3 locus.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep “dressed in black” in the main text and add an accessible textual note identifying the working “garments” reading as the conjecture attributed to Hilgenfeld in the supplied apparatus report, with “names” reported in A. Preserve the distinction between reported evidence and fresh manuscript verification. Review the new note independently.

findings.english_quote: The printed Athos-based text reconstructs the negative “would not” in damage.
findings.issue: The simplified conditional preserves the source's necessity and negation, and [f] discloses the supplied negative. However, the note omits the supplied apparatus's additional distinction between Anger's conjectural γεγόνεισαν and the reported Athos γεγόνασι. This leaves a relevant editorial choice in the final predicate undisclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Extend [f] with an attributed, reader-accessible account of the conjectural working verb and the different verb form reported in A. Do not substitute the variant automatically or weaken “would not have been useful.” Submit any revised note or English wording for fresh review.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all clauses of the selected working Greek. Their main texts preserve the names, counts, speaker changes, kingdom-entry contrast, reciprocal attachment of people and spirits, and final negative necessity claim. Revision is needed for two specific apparatus disclosures, not to replace the selected working readings. This assessment uses the supplied text and attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
